children.value: > Fact From Story The OLED panel in the new Steam Deck is lighter, thinner, and more power efficient than its LCD predecessor.
> > Fact From Story The new model squeezes a 7.4-inch OLED screen into the same space, significantly shrinking the bezels around the display.
> > > Fact From Story The panel has a wider color gamut (110% DCI-P3, for the visual obsessives) and the beautiful, inky blacks that OLED dorks like myself | Fact From Story
> > > Commonsense Knowledge A wider color gamut and inky blacks are desirable screen features. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge A bigger screen is an improvement.
> Fact From Story The Steam Deck OLED has longer battery life, faster Wi-Fi, and a stand-alone Bluetooth module.
> > Fact From Story The Steam Deck OLED has a die-shrunk version of the same custom APU found in the original Steam Deck.
> > > Fact From Story In concert with the more-efficient processor, there’s also a 25 percent larger battery with a 50Whr capacity, compared to the original’s 40Whr. | Fact From Story
> > > Fact From Story The new APU is produced on a 6nm process, rather than the older 7nm process. | Fact From Story
> > > Commonsense Knowledge A larger battery provides longer battery life. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge A die-shrunk chip uses less power.
> Commonsense Knowledge Improvements are better than what they improve upon.
